units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 24a:6">Kidd. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>בשן וע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="J00515"><he>יָצָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 24b:1">Ib. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>הכהו על עֵינוֹ וכ׳</he> if the master struck him on his eye and made it blind.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 83b:20">B. Kam. 83ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 21:24">Ex. XXI, 24</cite>) <he>אימא ע׳ ממש</he> may not the text mean that he who injures a person’s eye must really suffer the same injury? <cite ref="Shabbat 108b:13">Sabb. 108ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>יד לע׳ וכ׳</he> an unwashed hand (in the morning) touching the eye deserves to be cut off.
<cite ref="Taanit 8b:13">Taan. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>סמוי מן הע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="O01054"><he>סָמָא</he></cite>.

Ib. דבר שאין הע׳ שולטת בו something which the eye cannot look at (being stored away), v. infra; a. v. fr.—[Y. Ned. IX, end, 41ᶜ עשה לה ע׳ של זהב, a corrupt dittography of עשה לה שן של זהב.]—ע׳ טובה (also יפה) a benevolent eye, good will, liberality, opp. ע׳ רעה or עֵין הרע (abbr. עה״ר), also ע׳ צרה ill-will, selfishness, envy.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:9">Ab. II, 9</cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 74a:6">Sabb. 74ᵃ</cite> <he>משום ע׳ יפה וכ׳</he> he intended to show his good will.
<cite ref="Tosefta Challah 1:7">Tosef. Ḥall. I, 7</cite> <he>שעינו יפה בעיסתו</he> he is liberal with his dough (is glad to give the priest’s portion), opp. <he>עינו צרה</he>.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 2:2">Esth. R. to I, 4</cite> <he>היתה עינו צרה בממונו</he> he was jealous of his wealth (unwilling to leave it to his heirs to be enjoyed by them).

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:13">Ab. V, 13</cite> <he>עינו רצה בשל אחרים</he> he is illiberal with regard to other people’s money (begrudges them the privilege of giving charity), <he>ע׳ רעה בשלו</he> he is illiberal with his own money (is too greedy to afford himself the pleasure of giving charity).
Ib. II, 11, v. יֵצֶר; a. fr.—צַר ע׳ (= רַע ע׳) selfish, opp. טוב ע׳ liberal, selfless.
<cite ref="Shabbat 108b:12">Sabb. 108ᵇ</cite> <he>שדורי</he> … <he>צר ע׳ אנא</he> I send you (the salve), lest you say that I am selfish.
<cite ref="Sotah 38b:12">Sot. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>אפי׳ העופות מכירין בצָרֵי ע׳</he> even birds recognize selfish men.
<cite ref="Sotah 38b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>כל הנהנה מצרי ע׳ וכ׳</he> he who accepts benefits from self-seeking men, transgresses a law (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 23:6">Prov. XXIII, 6</cite>).

Ib. אין … לטוב ע׳ the cup of benediction must be handed to none but an unselfish person (with ref. to Prov. XXII, 9); a. e.—Esp. ע׳ רעה, עֵין הרע (abbrev. עה״ר), or only עַיִן, the evil eye, an envious glance that brings harm to the person looked at, bewitchment.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 107b:2">B. Mets. 107ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 7:15">Deut. VII, 15</cite>) <he>זו ע׳</he> that means the effect of an evil eye.
<cite ref="Deuteronomy 7:15">Ib.</cite> <he>תשעים … בע׳ רעה וכ׳</he> ninety-nine persons die of an evil eye against one in the natural course.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 91:6">Gen. R. s. 91</cite> <he>שלא תשלוט בכם עה״ר</he> that the evil eye may have no power over you.

Ib. לא הייתם … מפני הע׳ were you not afraid of the evil eye? Ber. 20a ע׳ שלא … אין עה״ר שולטת בי no evil eye can affect him whose eye refused to feed on what was not his (to look at the charms of a married woman); a. fr.—שקל ע׳ בע׳ to balance the scales exactly, to allow no overweight (v. עוּן, a. כָּרַע).
B. Bath. V, 11; a. fr.—בע׳ visible to the eye, discernible; in natural form.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1:6">Y. Ber. VI, 10ᵃ</cite> <he>אע״פ ששחוקין בעֵינָן הן</he> although they are ground, they are still discernible.

Ib. אם בעַיְינָן הן if they are in their natural form (not mashed); a. fr.—כְּעֵין like the appearance of, similar to, a sort of (cmp. גַּוָּון). Ib.ᵇ כל שהוא כע׳ סולת וכ׳ whatever resembles a pudding or dumpling.
Ber. 58ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) מלכותא דארעא כע׳ וכ׳ the government on earth is like the government in heaven (inspires reverence); a. fr.—מֵעֵין a reflection of, of the nature of; an abstract of.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 105b:13">Snh. 105ᵇ</cite> (ref. to the preposition <cite ref="M00000"><he>מ</he></cite> in <cite ref="I Kings 1:47">I Kings I, 47</cite>) <he>מע׳ קאמר ליה</he> he means, ‘as a reflection’ (of thy name, thy throne).
<cite ref="I Kings 1:47">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Judges 5:24">Jud. V, 24</cite>) <he>מע׳ קאמר</he> it means ‘similar to’ (the blessings of Sarah &c.).

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 4:3">Ber. IV, 3</cite> <he>מע׳ י״ח</he> an abstract of the eighteen benedictions. Y. ib. 8ᵃ bot. <he>שבע מע׳ י״ח</he> seven benedictions embodying the eighteen. Ib. VI, 10ᵇ <he>ברכה אחת מע׳ שלש</he> one benediction embodying the three.
Gen. R. s. 11, a. e., v. דּוּגְמַטְרִין.—Du. עֵינַיִים, עֵינַיִם.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 7:4">Bekh. VII, 4</cite> <he>עֵינָיו גדולות וכ׳</he> if his (the priest’s) eyes are as large as those of a calf.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 7:3">Ib. 3</cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 58a">Ber. 58ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>נתן עיניו בו וכ׳</he> he put his eyes on him, and he was turned into a heap of bones.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3:5:14">Y. Hor. III, end, 48ᶜ</cite> <he>נתנו עֵינֵיהֶן בשמואל וכ׳</he> they directed their attention to Samuel &c.; a. fr.—<he>אחז את הע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A01021"><he>אָחַז</he></cite>.

Kel. VIII, 7 ע׳ של תנור the ‘eye’ of an oven (the fire-place under the oven, Maim.; the opening for the escape of the smoke, which may be closed to retain the heat, R. S.). Ib. IX, 8 תנור שניקב מעינו an oven in the eye of which is a defect. Ib. XXI, 2 ע׳ the ring-shaped pad around an animal’s neck (a halter of soft material). Ib. ע׳ של מתכת a metal hame (cmp. עוֹנָתָא).
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 1:7">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. I, 7</cite> <he>העיין שבמצעד</he> the ring attached to an adze; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:10">Keth. I, 10</cite>; a. fr.—[Frequ. <cite ref="P00601"><he>עֵין</he></cite> in pr. n. pl., as <he>ע׳ סוכר</he>, <cite ref="P00553"><he>ע׳ טב</he></cite>; v. respective determinants].
